x: In the Shot Put Ted Gaworski gave us his usual Boxing Day exhibition of class putting. A stanger in this event was Ivan Mayers who made the most of his 3yd. 1ft.6in.
Ted Gaworski put the weight 43' 2" and the discus 135' 5" being 2nd in each event, whilst Percy Luxon won the Triple Jump with 45' 7" and the Long Jump with 20' 7".
Ted Gaworski seemed to have taken on too large a programme with three field events and in consequence his discus throwing late in the afternoon suffered badly.
Ash ran well to win the hurdles and was seen sailing over bars, both with and without a pole. Ted Gaworski won the shot. Mike Lyons, Mike Harris and newcomer Birdseye were our sprinters.
Ted Gaworski earned 3rd place for Surrey in the Shot Put with 44' 9". Percy Luxon, Middlesex, was not up to his best form and finished 5th in the Long Jump.

Luxon and Ted Gaworski were included in Franz Stampfl's team against Oxford and Cambridge and did very well. At Woodford Peter Porter threw the hammer for a new Club record of 157' 7" and Ted Gaworski put up another Club record in the weight.
Shot Put · T, Gaworski · do. · 46' 5"

Denis was also 2nd in the 100 yards and our other sprinters Mayers, Walden and Holtum all ran well in their heats of 100 and 220 yards. Ted Gaworski took 2nd place in the Shot put with a personal best and Mal Ash was 2nd in the High Jump and 5th in the hurdles.
Then Ted Gaworski improved on his weight performance by putting 44' 5" an increase of 1'7". Harris 2nd with 42 10" equalled the previous best and Ian Law was third with 39' 4".
Ted Gaworski won the weight with a first class putt of 45ft. 8inches, John Powell Jones was third with 43 feet 7 inches and Harris fifth with 43feet 1 inch.

Ivan Mayers reached the semi-final of the 220 yards in which he ran extremely well and Ted Gaworski gave his usual polished performances in the Shot and Discus, although not reaching the coveted placed positions.
Another outstanding field performance was that of T. Gaworski who won both the shot put and the discus, the latter with a new record for the meeting and a new club record of 147ft. 10ins.
The usual sterling performance came from Ted Gaworski who won the weight with 52ft. 9ins and the discus with 131ft. 1 in., and from Bob Harris who was second in both events.
Weight · T.J. Gaworski · August 1955 · 47ft 6½ins
It would be very nice to see Ted Gaworski and Dick Harris reach 50 feet and over in the weight. I am happy that Mal Ash will be giving us his valuable support this year.

Mal Ash helped our score along with a win in the Pole Vault with 12 feet, Harris was second in the weight, Ted Gaworski third in the Discus, Ron Liggins 6th in the Javelin, Percy Porter 5th in the Hammer - and the Sward Trophy was ours.
Coming back to our home county - Surrey; Ted Gaworski was a double winner in the discus and weight with a new county record for the former at 145ft. 4ins.

Saturday started with the discus and in this Ted Gaworski gained 4th place with 146ft 8ins and Harris gained a standard. In the 100 yards only Dennis Merrett qualified for the semi-final, winning his heat in 10.6.

Ted Gaworski's record in the Sward Meeting replaces the mark he set last July. The Junior Walk Record had stood to Jack Rutland for exactly 20 years until Terry Clark won the Surrey Junior Championship in the time given above.
Jones was first with 46ft. 3½ins., a championship best, with T.
Ted Gaworski gained a standard in the discus but Harris was not so fortunate. Mal Ash had a fall in the heat of the 120 yards hurdles when nicely placed and might well have done his best to date.
T.Gaworski.

Thames Valley Harriers started last year a Winter Field Events Meeting and again this year put on a similar meeting. Roy Liggins, Ted Gaworski and Percy Porter competed. Percy was 2nd in the Hammer and Ted was in the first six in the Discus.
Ted Gaworski was our man in the Discus and although pleading lack of training comparable with last year, when he took third place with 145'10", he was determined to do his best.
Ted Gaworski · 1st Surrey County Discus 134' 8"

We learn with regret that Ted Gaworski is in Maida Vale Hospital where he has been for three months following a serious illness, which has left him partially paralysed.
We have welcome news of Ted Gaworski in that he is back at work and progressing. He promises that he will be back on the Field at the earliest moment.

Yet another veteran best ever came from Mike Small and this time he removed the name of Ted Gaworski from our M40 record list; that discus record had stood since 1957!

Over a somewhat shorter distance Bob Taylor was 4th in the Southern AAA's 880 yards., Ted Gaworski was 2nd in the shot and 4th in discus. In the AAA's Jack Brown was 6th in the mile with the winner being Roger Bannister and at the same meeting Gordon Pirie set a new world six mile record of 28 mins…
On the track the Leyton Floodlit Meeting on a cold blustery evening saw Dennis Merrett, Ted Gaworski, John Bromley and Bob Taylor among a good Club turn out.
